newsitem.title: USA: U.S. manufacturers' profits rose in Q2.
newsitem.headline: U.S. manufacturers' profits rose in Q2.

text.p: After-tax profits of U.S. manufacturing companies averaged a seasonally adjusted 6.2 cents per dollar of sales in the second quarter of 1996, the Commerce Department said Friday.
That was up from 5.8 cents per dollar of sales in the first quarter. It was also higher than profits in the second quarter of 1995, which averaged a seasonally adjusted 5.9 cents per dollar of sales.
Total seasonally adjusted profits after taxes were $57.0 billion on net sales of $918.7 billion in the second quarter.
In the first quarter, profits were $52.8 billion on net sales of $906.8 billion. In the second quarter of last year, profits were $51.4 billion on net sales of $869.8 billion.
The report is based on quarterly financial reports from about 7,900 corporations, the department said.
After-tax profits of non-durable manufacturing companies rose to $30.4 billion in the second quarter of 1996 from $28.4 billion in the first quarter.
After-tax profits of durables manufacturers were up to $26.6 billion in the second quarter from $24.4 billion in the first quarter, the department said.
